name: PHILIPPINES

flag.title: Philippines Flag
flag.note: Blue, red, white — sun & three stars

lead: The Philippines is a jigsaw of 7,641 islands in the western Pacific. Volcanoes rumble, rice terraces climb misty mountains, and coral reefs teem with fish. Malay (Southeast Asian), Spanish and American history make it unlike anywhere else in Asia.
geo: The Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, with over 20 active volcanoes. Mayon Volcano has an almost perfect cone. Tiny Taal sits inside a lake.
On Palawan, you can paddle for kilometres through the Puerto Princesa Underground River cave. Bohol has over 1,260 smooth brown Chocolate Hills.
animals: The Philippine eagle has wings as wide as a classroom door. Tiny tarsiers, palm-sized primates (monkey relatives) with eyes bigger than their brains, cling to trees on Bohol.
Whale sharks visit Tubbataha Reef each spring. The tamaraw, a small wild buffalo, and the Visayan warty pig live nowhere else on Earth.
culture: Filipinos celebrate hundreds of fiestas a year. At the Ati-Atihan festival, dancers paint their faces and drum through the streets for days.
Adobo, meat simmered in vinegar, soy sauce and garlic, is the national dish. Filipinos take karaoke seriously, because singing together is how families show love.
history: King Philip II of Spain never visited, but the Philippines is named after him. Spain ruled it for 333 years from 1565. The USA took over in 1898.

The writer José Rizal's novels sparked a revolution, and he was put to death in 1896. Independence came in 1946. In 1986, People Power marchers toppled a dictator (all-powerful ruler) without firing a shot.
wows: Fewer than 2,000 of the 7,641 islands have names.
The Filipino language borrows words from Spanish, English, Malay and Chinese.
The Chocolate Hills turn brown in the dry season.
Killing a Philippine eagle can bring up to 12 years in prison, like many violent crimes.
Jeepneys, the colourful local buses, began as US Army jeeps left behind after World War II.
Christmas officially begins in September and lasts four months.
Taal is a volcano on an island in a lake on an island.

myths.fact: Baguio City sits 1,500 m up and can drop to 9 °C in January. People grow strawberries there.
Over 170 languages are spoken across the islands. Filipino and English link them all.
